records.text: Emily Ratajkowski wrote that after her divorce and during compulsive dating she adopted a sexual but frightening villain persona who was neither tragic nor a victim and whom others should envy.
records.speaker: Emily Ratajkowski

appearances.snippet: The character that I had learned to embody after my divorce, in my period of compulsively dating, was a villain. ... Poison Ivy, Catwoman, sexual but scary. And she drank gin martinis, many, many gin martinis. ... She was not tragic. She was nothing close to a victim. No one needed to feel sorry for her. In fact, they should all be jealous.

verification.notes: The original 2026 essay by Emily Ratajkowski contains the quoted post-divorce villain description, including Poison Ivy, Catwoman, sexual but scary, not tragic or a victim, and the statement that others should be jealous.

sources.title: Mother F*cker
sources.relevance: Original Emily Ratajkowski essay contains the quoted villain, sexual but scary, victim, and jealousy language.

records.text: Emily Ratajkowski wrote that she decided to use sexual encounters to make herself into a new kind of woman and said she did not care whether she was making many men suffer for one man's conduct.
records.speaker: Emily Ratajkowski

appearances.snippet: I decided to F my way into a new kind of woman. I wanted to destroy the Madonna, the special girl that I had worked so hard to be before an eight pound baby had torn my nether regions into two and replaced her with a, that's another word for slut that she has there that I don't want to say. ... And she writes, quote, let's give them a taste of their own medicine. I joke with friends. ... Was I punitive, making many men suffer for the crimes of one? ... I honestly didn't care.

verification.notes: The original 2026 essay contains both the decision to use sexual encounters to become a new kind of woman and the reflection about making many men suffer for the conduct of one man followed by not caring.
